title: Redwood POC scoping with Sterling Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a 4-week pilot: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, VPC option. Discussed success criteria (latency/throughput/cost), workload sizing and benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: send security pack, run benchmarks, schedule onboarding session.
next_steps: Redwood: send security pack (SOC 2, ISO certs, penetration test summary) by 2028-02-16
Redwood SE: run benchmark with customer sample dataset and share results by 2028-02-23
Customer: provide sample subset (10k records) and expected traffic patterns by 2028-02-16
Customer: confirm scope (hosted vs VPC) by 2028-02-21
action_items: Maya Chen (AE): send SOC2/ISO docs + security pack - due 2028-02-16
Ravi Patel (SE): run dedicated and hosted benchmarks with sample data, include p95/p99 latency and throughput - due 2028-02-23
Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng): share sample dataset and network topology (VPC peering details if choosing private) - due 2028-02-16
Priya Nair (Head of Security): review security pack and raise any compliance gaps - due 2028-02-20
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. We wanted to focus today's call on scoping the security pilot and align on success criteria and benchmarks. quick intro round?
[00:18] Tom Garcia (CTO): Yeah hi, Tom here, CTO at Sterling Health. Priya is our security lead, Liam handles infra, Sana is PM. We're looking to test Redwood for a secure inference layer for patient-facing triage and clinical summarization.
[00:36] Priya Nair (Head of Security): Hi all. Quick note up front: we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC with audit logs, and KMS-backed encryption. Also data residency in us-east-1 for the pilot.
[00:55] Ravi Patel (SE): Absolutely, thanks Priya. We can support hosted and VPC/private deployments. For the pilot we usually start with hosted with VPC peering or a private VPC depending on networking. We'll include KMS integration and audit log exports.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor (Platform Engineer): Quick question — when you say KMS integration, do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) or only Redwood-managed?
[01:22] Maya Chen (AE): Great Q. For hosted we support customer KMS integration on our enterprise plan; for Private deployments, you can bring your own HSM/KMS. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[01:35] Priya: Also need clarity on retention of logs and transcripts; default retention is fine but we need a 90-day export window and ability to turn off transcript retention for PII.
[01:48] Ravi: We can configure retention policies per customer, and we have audit log streams to S3 or your SIEM via webhook. There's an option for never-stored KV cache for sensitive prefixes, we'll mention that.
[02:05] Sana Ahmed (Product PM): On the success criteria side, our stakeholders want clear perf targets: p95 latency under 200ms for simple prompts, throughput to handle ~50 concurrent requests during peak, and cost per inference target around $X — we'll fill in exact numbers but ideally keep unit economics comparable to current infra.
[02:26] Maya: Perfect, typical pilot plan is 4 weeks: week 1 onboarding + infra setup, week 2 run benchmarks and initial integration, week 3 refine and run quality evals, week 4 decision and next steps. Does that fit your timeline?
[02:41] Tom: Yes, that's our expectation. We'll aim for decision within 4 weeks if benchmarks look good.
[02:49] Ravi: For benchmarks we'll need a representative sample. What does Sterling think is a good workload? average prompt length, expected generated tokens?
[02:58] Liam: For triage messages, prompts average 80 tokens, responses about 200 tokens. We expect around 100k tokens/day initially, ramp to 500k if we go to prod. Peak concurrent ~50-75.
[03:15] Ravi: Great, that's helpful. We'll size tests for 50 and then run a 2x stress run to 150 concurrent to see degradation. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput, and token/sec and GPU utilization for dedicated nodes.
[03:31] Priya: On compliance, please note we have an internal requirement for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence before running a pilot with real PHI-like data. Can you provide attestation and the scope?
[03:44] Maya: Yes — we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, and a security pack that includes our penetration test summary, architecture diagrams, and the list of controls. We'll also include our BAA template; if PHI is involved we'll need to get the BAA signed.
[03:59] Tom: BAA is essential, yes. Also data residency — must be able to keep data in us-east-1 for the pilot.
[04:08] Ravi: For hosted we can pin region to us-east-1; for Private you can host the control plane in your VPC. We'll note network egress encryption and VPC peering options.
[04:19] Sana: A couple of follow-ups on RBAC: we need role separation, ability to restrict model rollout to certain teams, and audit trails that show who invoked which routes, with token-level cost attribution.
[04:33] Ravi: We have RBAC with roles (admin, dev, viewer) and per-route permissions. Audit logs include request metadata, user, route, model version, and tokens consumed. Token-level cost attribution is part of the Console analytics.
[04:48] Priya: Do you store raw transcripts by default? and how do you handle PII redaction?
[04:55] Maya: By default we store transcripts for 30 days; it can be disabled. We also offer redaction hooks and can run custom redactors as part of the pipeline. We'll include the redaction options in the pack.
[05:08] Liam: Network question — if we do private deployment, what's the typical timeline for provisioning a dedicated cluster?
[05:15] Ravi: For Private on your VPC, initial provisioning is about 2-3 weeks depending on network approvals. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity), we can offer reserved GPU pools within 1-2 weeks if capacity available.
[05:28] Tom: For the pilot we prefer hosted pinned to region with VPC peering to reduce friction, unless there are blockers.
[05:36] Maya: That maps to our recommended path: start hosted pinned to us-east-1 with VP C peering and KMS integration, then decide if a Private roll is needed.
[05:46] Ravi: On benchmarks: we'll run both hosted and dedicated scenarios — we can run a small benchmark matrix: 1) hosted-cpu (if applicable), 2) hosted-gpu, 3) dedicated-1xA10 or equivalent, and 4) private if you choose. We'll provide raw logs and a summary sheet with p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost estimates.
[06:07] Sana: Can you also run quality regressions? we have a set of evaluation prompts that must not degrade beyond current baseline.
[06:13] Ravi: Yes — include eval harness. We'll run quality sets and provide BLEU-like and human sampling notes. We'll flag any regression.
[06:21] Priya: About pen tests — do you have a recent external pentest we can review?
[06:27] Maya: We have a third-party pentest summary from last quarter. We'll include high-level findings and remediations in the pack, and if you require a custom pentest we can coordinate with our security team and give guidance for scope.
[06:40] Tom: Great. pricing — for the pilot, do you provide a credit or trial pricing?
[06:45] Maya: We generally offer pilot credits and can scope a limited-time discount for the pilot. We'll put that in the pricing note. Also, we'll show cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated in the benchmark sheet.
[06:58] Liam: One more networking detail — we use strict egress rules; will Redwood require inbound rules from your side?
[07:05] Ravi: For VPC peering we'll need a peering connection and specific CIDR ranges; for webhooks and audit exports we can use outbound to your S3 with signed URLs or an IP allowlist. We'll include a network runbook.
[07:17] Sana: Recap on success criteria — to be explicit: 1) p95 latency < 200ms for standard triage prompts; 2) handle 50 concurrent with linear degradation up to 150; 3) quality parity within X% of baseline (we'll provide baseline); 4) SOC2/ISO + BAA in place; 5) reasonable cost per inference — decision to proceed to contract after week 4.
[07:44] Maya: Yup, we'll capture that. For the cost target, can you provide a ballpark $/1000 tokens you expect as acceptable?
[07:52] Tom: I'd say keep it below $Y per 1k tokens — we'll fill exact numbers in the follow-up.
[07:58] Priya: Also note: audit retention policy — we need 12 months of immutable audit for certain actions, and 90 days for request transcripts. Can you keep immutable audit exports to our S3?
[08:10] Ravi: Yes we can stream immutable audit logs to your S3 with encryption using your KMS key. We'll document that in the runbook.
[08:20] Tom: Ok sounds good. What's the timeline for the benchmark run?
[08:25] Ravi: If we get sample data and the network/access by 2028-02-16, SE team will run benchmarks and deliver results by 2028-02-23.
[08:33] Sana: We'll aim to provide data and the compliance point of contact this week.
[08:38] Maya: Perfect. Any blockers for the BAA signature?
[08:41] Priya: We'll have Legal review; expect comments but shouldn't block pilot start if we use redacted test data.
[08:50] Ravi: Small note on KV cache and sensitive prefixes — if you have tokens you don't want cached, we can disable prefix caching per-route.
[08:59] Liam: Good — we have a few templates that can't be cached. We'll share the list.
[09:05] Maya: All right, let's walk through the weekly plan briefly so everyone is aligned. Week 1: onboarding and connectivity, week 2: benchmarks + quality evals, week 3: integration and iterate, week 4: decision and contract discussion.
[09:22] Tom: Works for us.
[09:26] Priya: Can you also include SOC 2 scope mapping to our internal controls? 
[09:31] Maya: Yes we'll include a mapping doc showing which Redwood controls map to your policies.
[09:36] Sana: for the benchmark, include p99 spikes and tail latency graphs — those will be critical for clinical use.
[09:44] Ravi: Absolutely. We'll include dashboards and raw traces.
[09:48] Tom: Anything else?
[09:51] Maya: One last ask — we'll follow up with the security pack + BAA + network runbook and a small test plan. Expect email by EOD 2028-02-16.
[10:01] Priya: Thanks, appreciate it.
[10:04] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and action items.
[10:08] Tom: Thanks, bye.
[10:10] End of call.

Notes: transcript includes typical filler and occasional mis-attributions from auto-transcribe. References: shared links to security pack, benchmark sheet, BAA template (links to be attached in follow-up email).
